key_insight: The paper builds a non-intrusive reduced-order model that adapts radial basis functions to local attractor geometry, enabling chaotic-flow predictions that preserve long-term statistics.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical surrogate modeling route for turbulent and chaotic systems when governing equations are unavailable or too expensive to project directly.
method: Cluster the low-dimensional attractor into regions with distinct local geometry.
Fit a single regularized least-squares radial-basis vector field with region-adapted kernels.
Use a kinematic corrector to stabilize trajectories that drift away from the learned manifold.
evidence_signal: Across Lorenz-63, Lorenz-96, Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, and Kolmogorov flow, the model reproduces invariant measures, attractor structure, spectra, and key Lyapunov behavior, with competitive valid prediction time.
watch_item: Because the radial basis field decays away from training data, trajectory stabilization depends on the corrector, so the reported performance should be interpreted together with corrector magnitude and training coverage.
paper_title: Manifold-adapted radial basis functions for reduced-order modelling of chaotic flows
